arxiv-2111-08305.title: Two body dynamics in a quadratic modification of general relativity
arxiv-2111-08305.creator: Soham Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2111-08305.description: Abstract It is shown in this study that deviations from the Einstein-Hilbert action at the quadratic level using a proper analyses and suitable dynamical variables lead to a tiny modification to the post Newtonian equations of motion, and non-GR like behavior at very short length scales.

arxiv-2112-12679.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xin Tong. Abstract This is our second scope of the consideration on the corresponding topologization and the corresponding functional analytification. We will focus on the corresponding functorial and motivic constructions in our current consideration.

arxiv-2301-07231.title: Chirality Dependent Photon Transport and Helical Superradiance
arxiv-2301-07231.creator: Jonah S. Peter, Stefan Ostermann, Susanne F. Yelin
arxiv-2301-07231.description: Abstract Chirality, or handedness, is a geometrical property denoting a lack of mirror symmetry. Chirality is ubiquitous in nature and is associated with the non-reciprocal interactions observed in complex systems ranging from biomolecules to topological materials. Here, we demonstrate that chiral arrangements of dipole-coupled atoms or molecules can facilitate the unidirectional transport of helical photonic excitations without breaking time-reversal symmetry.

arxiv-2303-00940.title: Sampling over Union of Joins
arxiv-2303-00940.creator: Yurong Liu, Yunlong Xu, Fatemeh Nargesian
arxiv-2303-00940.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yurong Liu, Yunlong Xu, Fatemeh Nargesian. Data scientists often draw on multiple relational data sources for analysis. A standard assumption in learning and approximate query answering is that the data is a uniform and independent sample of the underlying distribution. To avoid the cost of join and union, given a set of joins, we study the problem of obtaining a random sample from the union of joins without performing the full join and union.

arxiv-2310-11555.title: Integrating 3D City Data through Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2310-11555.creator: Linfang Ding, Guohui Xiao, Albulen Pano, Mattia Fumagalli, Dongsheng Chen, Yu Feng, Diego Calvanese, Hongchao Fan, Liqiu Meng
arxiv-2310-11555.description: Abstract CityGML is a widely adopted standard by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) for representing and exchanging 3D city models. The representation of semantic and topological properties in CityGML makes it possible to query such 3D city data to perform analysis in various applications, e.g., security management and emergency response, energy consumption and estimation, and occupancy measurement.

arxiv-2407-13998.title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
arxiv-2407-13998.creator: Rujun Han Yuhao Zhang Peng Qi Yumo Xu Jenyuan Wang, Lan Liu William Yang Wang Bonan Min Vittorio Castelli
arxiv-2407-13998.description: Abstract Question answering based on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG-QA) is an important research topic in NLP and has a wide range of real-world applications. However, most existing datasets for this task are either constructed using a single source corpus or consist of short extractive answers, which fall short of evaluating large language model (LLM) based RAG-QA systems on cross-domain generalization.

arxiv-2505-17614.title: PathoSCOPE: Few-Shot Pathology Detection via Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning and Pathology-Informed Synthetic Embeddings
arxiv-2505-17614.creator: Sinchee Chin, Yinuo Ma, Xiaochen Yang, Jing-Hao Xue, Wenming Yang
arxiv-2505-17614.description: Abstract Unsupervised pathology detection trains models on non-pathological data to flag deviations as pathologies, offering strong generalizability for identifying novel diseases and avoiding costly annotations. However, building reliable normality models requires vast healthy datasets, as hospitals’ data is inherently biased toward symptomatic populations, while privacy regulations hinder the assembly of representative healthy cohorts.

arxiv-2507-16750.title: Global Finite Energy Solutions of the Maxwell-Scalar Field System on the Einstein Cylinder
arxiv-2507-16750.creator: Jean-Philippe Nicolas, Grigalius Taujanskas
arxiv-2507-16750.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jean-Philippe Nicolas, Grigalius Taujanskas. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global finite energy solutions of the Maxwell-scalar field system in Lorenz gauge on the Einstein cylinder ℝ × 𝕊 3 \mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3} . Our method is a combination of a conformal patching argument, the finite energy existence theorem in Lorenz gauge on Minkowski space of Selberg and Tesfahun, a careful localization of finite energy data, and null form estimates of Foschi–Klainerman type.

arxiv-2508-17808.title: The sub-Riemannian geometry of measurement based quantum computation
arxiv-2508-17808.creator: Lukas Hantzko, Arnab Adhikary, Robert Raussendorf
arxiv-2508-17808.description: Abstract The computational power of symmetry-protected phases of matter can be accessed through local measurements, but what is the most efficient way of doing so? In this work, we show that minimizing operational resources in measurement-based quantum computation on subsystem symmetric resource states amounts to solving a sub-Riemannian geodesic problem between the identity and the target logical unitary.

arxiv-2601-22510.title: Shattered Compositionality: Counterintuitive Learning Dynamics of Transformers for Arithmetic
arxiv-2601-22510.creator: Xingyu Zhao, Darsh Sharma, Rheeya Uppaal, Yiqiao Zhong
arxiv-2601-22510.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit unexpected errors or unintended behavior, even at scale. While recent work reveals the discrepancy between LLMs and humans in skill compositions, the learning dynamics of skill compositions and the underlying cause of non-human behavior remain elusive. In this study, we investigate the mechanism of learning dynamics by training transformers on synthetic arithmetic tasks.

pmc-12548260.title: Mechanical assessment of a titanium cervical spine corpectomy cage assembled with 3D-printed patient-specific endplate-conformed contact surfaces and a traditionally manufactured expandable mechanism
pmc-12548260.creator: Shih-Chieh Shen, Shao-Fu Huang, Wei-Hsiang Sun, Chun-Li Lin
pmc-12548260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study developed a new titanium cervical spine expandable corpectomy cage (ECC) that consisted of two superior/inferior patient-specific endplate-conformed contact surfaces (PECSs) fabricated through 3D printing and a standardized centrally expandable mechanism (CEM) manufactured using traditional machining. Fatigue testing was conducted to evaluate whether the components of ECC could be assembled using different manufacturing methods to meet the functional testing requirements in compliance with FDA regulations.

pmc-12577121.title: 16p13.11 microduplication in 14 fetuses: prenatal diagnosis and postnatal follow-up
pmc-12577121.creator: Yuchun Pan, Yu Hu, Chonglan Gao, Han Kang, Yifei Chen, Lingxi Wang
pmc-12577121.description: Background16p13.11 Microduplication is a rare genetic disorder with variable expression and incomplete penetrance, primarily reported in adults and children, with limited information available on fetal cases. This study aims to analyze the characteristics of prenatal diagnosis indications and postnatal follow-up in fetuses with 16p13.11 microduplication, and to explore the genotype-phenotype correlation for improving genetic counseling and patients’ care.

pmc-12732018.title: Effect of CaCl2-Induced Surface Gelatinization on Enzymatic Porous Starch
pmc-12732018.creator: Nianxia Sun, Yakun Wang, Jie Zhang, Zesheng Wu, Mengting Cheng, Hui Shen, Dianlei Wang, Bo Cui
pmc-12732018.description: Porous starch (PS) is widely used in food, pharmaceutical, and environmental industries for its high adsorption capacity and controlled release properties. To explore how surface gelatinization affected enzymatically prepared PS, corn starch was first modified via surface gelatinization using a CaCl2 solution and then treated with α-amylase and amyloglucosidase to synthesize PS. Its structural and functional characteristics were subsequently analyzed.

pmc-12930740.description: BackgroundPermanent tooth loss is a key feature of non-syndromic tooth agenesis (NSTA). However, whether this is influenced by the mandibular environment remains unclear.
